verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Rajkot castings and forgings units with export order books and conservative gearing; avoid single-customer CV-dependent units with weak balance sheets.
title: Rajkot Castings & Forgings: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Rajkot foundry melts scrap and ingots, pours them into moulds, machines the casting or forging, and sells to auto, CV, tractor and industrial buyers.** Cash comes in only after the buyer accepts the lot, so the unit funds scrap inventory, furnace power, wages and machining before a rupee returns. **Power and scrap are the two big cost lines and neither is priced by the borrower** — so when a proposal lands, check the power tariff contract and the scrap sourcing arrangement before anything else.

## Where value and cash actually sit
**Value sits in the machining and finishing step, not in raw pouring** — a unit that only pours competes on price and earns thin margins. Peer evidence: Nelcast reported revenue of Rs 335 crore in Q2FY25 against Rs 362.6 crore in Q2FY24, with topline muted on subdued domestic and export CV demand [4]. **Margins improve when raw material softens, not when volumes rise** — one peer's OPM rose to 8.4% in FY2025 from 7.5% in FY2024 on softening raw material prices even as revenue fell about 2% [11]. So when a proposal lands, check whether the margin story is volume-led or input-price-led; if it is input-led, ask what happens when scrap turns.

## What has changed now
**The national picture is soft but not broken: IIP for NIC 24 output is +2.4% YoY and +3.4% Apr-to-date [D].** Gujarat is running ahead of India on collections — GST +11.9% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D] — and electricity demand +11.0% versus India +9.5% [D], which tells us local activity is holding. **The peer set is split, and that split is the credit story.** Ramkrishna Forgings grew revenue 54.9% YoY to Rs 1,405 crore in Q2 FY27 with EBITDA margin at 18.23% and Rs 673 crore of new orders [6]; Happy Forgings carries an order book of nearly Rs 950 crore to be executed over the next 2-3 years, about 60% export [5]. Against that, Nelcast's CV-linked topline stayed muted [4]. **The local sources say little about Rajkot's own order books** — the Castings & Foundries Expo India is scheduled at NSIC Ground, Rajkot, from Nov 25-28, 2026 [1], and that is essentially all we have; treat first principles and peers as the base. Note also that a Rajkot-focused NPA and loan-settlement advisory page exists [2] — a reminder that stressed units in this cluster are already being worked out.

## Who to pursue now, and how to grow safely
**Pursue the export-order and non-CV industrial borrower, and the machining-integrated unit.** Ask for the order book split between export and domestic CV; if export is the majority, ask for the buyer-wise ageing and the forex cover. **Structure to the working-capital cycle, not to the furnace capacity** — cash credit against stock and book debts, with a clear drawing-power formula on accepted receivables. **Take every month: stock-and-debt statement, power bill, and the top-five buyer sales register.** Covenant on gearing and interest coverage; a peer with gearing close to nil and TOL/TNW at 0.3 times shows what a strong balance sheet in this trade looks like [8]. **Avoid the single-customer CV-dependent unit and the borrower whose only edge is price** — Nelcast's muted CV topline [4] is the warning. Where a rating exists, read it: Simplex Castings carries Crisil BB/Stable with Rs 72 crore of rated bank facilities [9], and Arcvac Forgecast's Total Debt/GCA improved from 3.49x in FY22 to 1.56x in FY23 with no planned debt-funded capex near term [10] — that is the shape of a lendable file.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days against the buyer mix, monthly.** If export receivables stretch while domestic CV orders fall, cut drawing power before the quarter closes. **Watch power cost per tonne and furnace running hours** — a unit running fewer hours than stated capacity is losing orders, not saving cost. **Watch for a shift from machined to raw casting sales** — that is margin walking out of the door. **Watch any request to fund capacity expansion while the existing order book is flat** — the Arcvac file shows expansion is fine when debt is not funding it [10].
watch: Receivable days rise beyond the sanctioned cycle -> reduce drawing power and ask for buyer-wise ageing
Monthly power bill and running hours
Furnace hours fall below stated capacity for two months -> ask for order book and visit the unit
Machined share falls and raw casting share rises -> reprice the limit and tighten margin covenant
Single buyer crosses a concentration threshold -> seek additional collateral or a buyer diversification plan
Gearing rises or coverage falls below covenant -> freeze fresh limits and restructure
